items.title: TailwindHelper
items.text: MODX Helper for Tailwind.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• MODX Revolution 2.8+
  • PHP 7.2+

items.title: Features
items.text: With this MODX Revolution extra all used CSS classes in chunks, templates, resources, template variables, ContentBlocks templates and files in configurable folders are collected and saved to a safelist.json file. This safelist can be used to avoid purging the used CSS classes in a MODX installation.

items.title: Changelog
items.text:
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Scan the default values of template variables, the files of static resources and the files of template variable @FILE bindings
  • Detect the classes in Alpine.js x-bind:class attributes and in MODX tag properties with class or cls in their name like &hereClass

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Scan all text files in the tailwindhelper.filepaths folders and skip the sub folders that can't be read
  • Restrict the menu entry and the scan to manager users with the settings permission
  • Don't expose server paths in the manager page options

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• Find the classes in class attributes with line breaks or escaped quotes (i.e. in JSON, nested MIGX values or PHP strings), in output modifiers with multiple or nested classes and in If snippet &then and &else values
  • Keep Tailwind classes with [[ in arbitrary values like grid-cols-[[full-start]_1fr]
  • Read the files of static chunks and templates and all ContentBlocks templates: inline, @FILE and @PDO_FILE templates and the template properties of the fields
  • Write the safelist.json reliably: skip classes that are not valid UTF-8 instead of writing an empty file, show the write errors and use the right default folder
  • Enable the buttons of the scan console window, if the scan fails

items.title: Install from MODX Extras
items.text: Search for TailwindHelper in the Package Manager of your MODX installation and install it in there.

items.title: Manual installation
items.text:
If you can't access the MODX Extras Repository in your MODX installation, you can manually install TailwindHelper.

  • Download the transport package from MODX Extras (or one of the pre built transport packages in _packages)
  • Upload the zip file to your MODX installation's core/packages folder or upload it manually in the MODX Package Manager.
  • In the MODX Manager, navigate to the Package Manager page, and select 'Search locally for packages' from the dropdown button.
  • TailwindHelper should now show up in the list of available packages. Click the corresponding 'Install' button and follow the instructions to complete the installation.

items.title: Build it from source
items.text: To build and install the package from source you could use Git Package Management. The GitHub repository of TailwindHelper contains a config.json to build that package locally. Use this option, if you want to debug TailwindHelper and/or contribute bugfixes and enhancements.

items.title: Menu Entry
items.text:
To generate a safelist.json file, you simply have to click on the TailwindHelper menu entry in the Extras menu. TailwindHelper collects the CSS classes in the content of:

  • chunks
  • templates
  • resources
  • template variable default values
  • template variable values of the resources
  • ContentBlocks field and layout templates, if ContentBlocks is installed
  • text files in the folders of the tailwindhelper.filepaths system setting

For static chunks and templates, the content of the static file is scanned. For static resources, the content of their file is scanned, if it is a text file. Template variable values and default values with a @FILE binding are read from the file.

The target path of the safelist.json can be changed with the tailwindhelper.safelistFolder system setting. The menu entry is only shown to manager users with the settings permission.

items.title: Detected Classes
items.text:
The CSS classes are detected in:

  • standard class="whatever" attributes
  • Alpine.js :class="{ 'whatever': variable === 'foo' }" and x-bind:class attributes. All strings in single quotes are added, so this example will add whatever and foo to the detected classes.
  • Alpine.js x-transition attributes like x-transition:enter="whatever"
  • properties of MODX tags with class or cls in their name like [[$chunk? &cls=`whatever`]] or the &hereClass, &rowClass and &outerClass properties of menu snippets. xPDO class names in the &class property of snippets like pdoResources are skipped.

The attributes are also detected with escaped quotes like class=\"whatever\" in JSON encoded HTML (i.e. in MIGX template variable values) or in PHP and JavaScript strings. Quotes, that are escaped multiple times like in nested MIGX values, are detected too.

The class names are separated by whitespace and included in the list as individual classes.

MODX tags in the class attributes are handled as well. The classes in the values of output modifiers like [[+placeholder:notempty=`whatever`]] (then, else, notempty, isnotempty, ifnotempty, !empty, empty, isempty, ifempty and default) and in the &then and &else properties of If snippet calls are added to the detected classes. Other MODX tags like [[+placeholder]] are removed from the list, if the tailwindhelper.removeModxTags system setting is enabled.

A MODX tag in a longer class like bg-[[+color]] is kept as part of that class. With the tailwindhelper.removeModxTags system setting enabled, the whole class is removed from the list. Tailwind arbitrary values with [[ like grid-cols-[[full-start]_1fr] are no MODX tags and stay in the list.

items.title: System Settings
items.text:
TailwindHelper uses the following system settings in the namespace tailwindhelper:

Key Name Description Default tailwindhelper.debug Debug Log debug information in the MODX error log. No tailwindhelper.filepaths File Paths Comma-separated list of folders that are recursively searched for text files (e.g. HTML, PHP, JavaScript, JSON, XML or SVG files). The content of these files is searched for CSS classes for the safelist.json. The placeholders {core_path}, {base_path} and {assets_path} can be used. - tailwindhelper.removeModxTags Remove MODX Tags Remove the classes with MODX tags from the safelist.json. Yes tailwindhelper.safelistFolder Safelist Folder The folder of the safelist.json. The placeholders {core_path}, {base_path} and {assets_path} can be used. {core_path}components/tailwindhelper/elements/purge/

items.title: Example usage
items.text: The created safelist.json has to be referenced in your Tailwind configuration, so that the used CSS classes are not removed from the build. The examples use the default location of the safelist.json. Change the path, if you have changed the tailwindhelper.safelistFolder system setting.

items.title: Tailwind 4
items.text:
Tailwind 4 scans the files in an @source directive for class names. Add the safelist.json as a source in your main CSS file. The path is relative to that CSS file:

@import "tailwindcss";
@source "./path-to-your-core/core/components/tailwindhelper/elements/purge/safelist.json";

items.title: Tailwind 3
items.text:
Reference the safelist.json in the safelist option of the tailwind.config.js:

const safelist = require('./path-to-your-core/core/components/tailwindhelper/elements/purge/safelist.json').concat([
    'additional-class'
]);

module.exports = {
    content: ['./src/**/*.html'],
    safelist: safelist,
    // your other options
};

items.title: Tailwind 2
items.text:
Tailwind 2 removes the unused classes with PurgeCSS in a production build. Reference the safelist.json in the purge.options.safelist option of the tailwind.config.js:

const safelist = require('./path-to-your-core/core/components/tailwindhelper/elements/purge/safelist.json').concat([
    'additional-class'
]);

module.exports = {
    purge: {
        content: ['./src/**/*.html'],
        options: {
            safelist: safelist
        }
    },
    // your other options
};
